entries.final: You are all wanderers in this world. Go north, south, west, or east—wherever you stop, there will be someone who drives you away, saying: “This is my land.” And, having gone around all the countries of the world, you will return having learned that nowhere is there a miserable piece of land where your wife could give birth, where you could stop to cultivate the land, and where your children could bury your bones.

entries.russian: Бросить человека посреди Атлантического океана, сказав ему, что он волен идти на берег, было бы не большим издевательством над ним, чем помещение его на земле, сплошь захваченной в частную собственность, сказав ему при этом, что он — свободный человек, волен работать на себя и пользоваться своим заработком.
entries.site_before: To throw a man in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, telling him he is free to go ashore, would not be a greater mockery of him than placing him on land entirely taken as private property, telling him at the same time that he is a free man, free to work for himself and enjoy his earnings.
entries.repo_before: To throw a person into the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, telling him that he is free to go to shore, would be no greater mockery of him than placing him on land wholly taken into private property, while telling him that he is a free man, free to work for himself and make use of his earnings.
entries.final: To throw a person into the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, telling him that he is free to go to shore, would be no greater mockery of him than placing him on land wholly taken into private property, while telling him that he is a free man, free to work for himself and make use of his earnings.

entries.russian: Незаконное право земельной собственности лишило больше, чем половину людей каждого народа их естественного наследия.
entries.site_before: The illegal right to land ownership has deprived more than half of the people of every nation of their natural inheritance.
entries.repo_before: The unlawful right of property in land has deprived more than half the people of every nation of their natural inheritance.
entries.final: The unlawful right of property in land has deprived more than half the people of every nation of their natural inheritance.

entries.russian: Поместите сто человек на острове, из которого нет выхода, и сделаете ли вы одного из этих людей полным властелином над остальными 99, или полным властелином земли всего острова, не будет никакой разницы.
entries.site_before: Place a hundred people on an island from which there is no escape, and whether you make one of these people the complete ruler over the other 99, or the complete master of the land of the entire island, it will make no difference.
entries.repo_before: Place a hundred people on an island from which there is no exit, and whether you make one of these people absolute master over the other ninety-nine, or absolute master of all the land on the island, there will be no difference.
entries.final: Place a hundred people on an island from which there is no exit, and whether you make one of these people absolute master over the other 99, or absolute master of all the land on the island, there will be no difference.
entries.reason: Repo wording, keeping the numeral 99 as printed.

entries.russian: Разве это не рабство, что хотя в Англии довольно земли, чтобы содержать в десять раз больше людей, чем теперь, все-таки многие должны просить милостыню у своих братьев, или тяжело работать за поденную плату, или умирать с голода, воровать, или быть повешенными, как люди, недостойные жить на земле.
entries.site_before: Is it not slavery that although in England there is enough land to sustain ten times more people than now, still many must beg from their brothers, or work hard for daily wages, or starve, steal, or be hanged as people unworthy to live on the land?
entries.repo_before: Is it not slavery that although in England there is enough land to support ten times more people than now, still many must beg alms from their brothers, or labor hard for day wages, or die of hunger, steal, or be hanged as people unworthy to live on the earth.
entries.final: Is it not slavery that although in England there is enough land to support ten times more people than now, still many must beg alms from their brothers, or labor hard for day wages, or die of hunger, steal, or be hanged as people unworthy to live on the earth.

entries.russian: Право на собственность земли означает голод, жажду, отсутствие одежд, труд, потраченный даром, захват произведений готового труда, уничтожение домов, нищету, болезни, смерть родителей, детей, жен, отчаяние и одичание в сердцах бедных, когда законная сила поражает их в самые чувствительные и жизненные права человечества. Всё это заключается в праве земельной собственности.
entries.site_before: The right to own land means hunger, thirst, lack of clothing, labor wasted in vain, seizure of the results of others' labor, destruction of houses, poverty, disease, death of parents, children, wives, despair and savagery in the hearts of the poor when legitimate authority strikes them in the most sensitive and vital rights of humanity. All this is included in the right to land ownership.
entries.repo_before: The right of property in land means hunger, thirst, lack of clothing, labor spent in vain, seizure of the products of completed labor, destruction of homes, poverty, sickness, death of parents, children, wives, despair and brutalization in the hearts of the poor when legal force strikes them in the most sensitive and vital rights of humanity. All this is contained in the right of landed property.
entries.final: The right of property in land means hunger, thirst, lack of clothing, labor spent in vain, seizure of the products of completed labor, destruction of homes, poverty, sickness, death of parents, children, wives, despair and brutalization in the hearts of the poor when legal force strikes them in the most sensitive and vital rights of humanity. All this is contained in the right of landed property.

entries.russian: Тот, кто владеет земельной собственностью в большем размере того, что нужно ему для пропитания своего и своей семьи, не только участник, но и виновник той нужды, тех бедствий и того развращения, от которых страдают народные массы.
entries.site_before: He who owns land in greater measure than what he needs to provide for himself and his family is not only a participant but also the cause of that need, those misfortunes, and that corruption from which the masses suffer.
entries.repo_before: The person who owns landed property in greater measure than is needed to support himself and his family is not only a participant in, but a cause of, the want, the calamities, and the corruption from which the masses of the people suffer.
entries.final: The person who owns landed property in greater measure than is needed to support himself and his family is not only a participant in, but a cause of, the want, the calamities, and the corruption from which the masses of the people suffer.

entries.russian: Пришли две женщины к старцу за поучением. Одна считала себя великой грешницей. Она в молодости изменила мужу и не переставая мучилась. Другая же, прожив всю жизнь по закону, ни в каком особенном грехе не упрекала себя и была довольна собой.
entries.site_before: Two women came to an elder for guidance. One considered herself a great sinner. In her youth, she had been unfaithful to her husband and was constantly tormented by it. The other, having lived her entire life according to the law, had never accused herself of any particular sin and was satisfied with herself.
entries.repo_before: Two women came to an elder for instruction. One considered herself a great sinner. In her youth she had been unfaithful to her husband and never ceased tormenting herself. The other, having lived all her life according to the law, did not reproach herself with any particular sin and was satisfied with herself.
entries.final: Two women came to an elder for instruction. One considered herself a great sinner. In her youth she had been unfaithful to her husband and never ceased tormenting herself. The other, having lived all her life according to the law, did not reproach herself with any particular sin and was satisfied with herself.

entries.russian: Старец расспросил обеих женщин об их жизни. Одна со слезами призналась ему в своем великом грехе. Она считала свой грех столь великим, что не ожидала за него прощения; другая же сказала, что не знает за собой никаких особенных грехов. Старец сказал первой:
entries.site_before: The elder asked both women about their lives. One tearfully confessed her great sin to him. She considered her sin so great that she did not expect forgiveness for it; the other said she did not know of any particular sins of her own. The elder said to the first:
entries.repo_before: The elder questioned both women about their lives. One confessed her great sin to him with tears. She considered her sin so great that she did not expect forgiveness for it; the other said that she knew of no particular sins in herself. The elder said to the first:
entries.final: The elder questioned both women about their lives. One confessed her great sin to him with tears. She considered her sin so great that she did not expect forgiveness for it; the other said that she knew of no particular sins in herself. The elder said to the first:

entries.russian: — Поди ты, раба божья, за ограду и найди ты мне большой камень — такой, какой поднять можешь, и принеси... А ты, — сказал он той, которая не знала за собой больших грехов, — принеси мне тоже каменьев, сколько осилишь, только всё мелких.
entries.site_before: — Go, you servant of God, beyond the fence and find me a large stone — one that you can lift, and bring it... And you, — he said to the one who did not know of great sins — bring me stones as well, as many as you can carry, only all small ones.
entries.repo_before: — Go, servant of God, beyond the fence and find me a large stone—as large as you can lift—and bring it... And you, — he said to the one who knew of no great sins in herself, — bring me stones too, as many as you can manage, but all small ones.
entries.final: — Go, servant of God, beyond the fence and find me a large stone—as large as you can lift—and bring it... And you, — he said to the one who knew of no great sins in herself, — bring me stones too, as many as you can manage, but all small ones.

entries.russian: Женщины пошли и исполнили приказание старца. Одна принесла большой камень, другая полный мешок мелких каменьев.
entries.site_before: The women went and carried out the elder's command. One brought a large stone, the other a sack full of small stones.
entries.repo_before: The women went and carried out the elder's instruction. One brought a large stone, the other a full bag of small stones.
entries.final: The women went and carried out the elder's instruction. One brought a large stone, the other a full bag of small stones.

entries.russian: — Теперь вот что сделайте: снесите вы назад камни и положите на те самые места, где взяли, и когда положите, приходите ко мне.
entries.site_before: — Now do this: carry the stones back and place them in the exact spots where you took them from, and when you have placed them, come to me.
entries.repo_before: — Now do this: take the stones back and put them in the very places where you took them, and when you have put them back, come to me.
entries.final: — Now do this: take the stones back and put them in the very places where you took them, and when you have put them back, come to me.

entries.russian: И женщины пошли исполнять приказание старца. Первая легко нашла то место, с которого взяла камень, и положила его, как он был; но другая никак не могла вспомнить, с какого места брала какой камень и так, не исполнив приказания, с тем же мешком каменьев вернулась к старцу.
entries.site_before: And the women went to carry out the elder's command. The first easily found the spot from which she had taken the stone and placed it as it was; but the other could not remember from which spot she had taken each small stone and, without fulfilling the command, returned to the elder with the same sack of stones.
entries.repo_before: And the women went to carry out the elder's instruction. The first easily found the place from which she had taken the stone and put it back as it had been; but the other could not remember which stone she had taken from which place and so, without carrying out the instruction, returned to the elder with the same bag of stones.
entries.final: And the women went to carry out the elder's instruction. The first easily found the place from which she had taken the stone and put it back as it had been; but the other could not remember which stone she had taken from which place and so, without carrying out the instruction, returned to the elder with the same bag of stones.
entries.reason: E1: the site added "small"; the Russian says "which stone".

entries.russian: — Так вот, — сказал старец, — то же бывает и с грехами. Ты легко положила большой и тяжелый камень на прежнее место, потому что помнила, откуда взяла его.
entries.site_before: — So, — the elder said, — the same happens with sins. You easily placed the large and heavy stone back in its original place because you remembered where you took it from.
entries.repo_before: — So there you are, — said the elder, — the same thing happens with sins. You easily put the large, heavy stone back in its former place because you remembered where you had taken it from.
entries.final: — So there you are, — said the elder, — the same thing happens with sins. You easily put the large, heavy stone back in its former place because you remembered where you had taken it from.

entries.russian: — А ты не могла, потому что не помнила, где взяла мелкие камни.
entries.site_before: — But you couldn't because you did not remember where you had taken the small stones from.
entries.repo_before: — But you could not, because you did not remember where you had taken the small stones.
entries.final: — But you could not, because you did not remember where you had taken the small stones.

entries.russian: — Ты помнила свой грех, несла за него укоры людей и своей совести, смирялась и потому освобождалась от последствий греха.
entries.site_before: — You remembered your sin, bore the reproaches of people and your own conscience for it, humbled yourself and therefore were freed from the consequences of sin.
entries.repo_before: — You remembered your sin, bore for it the reproaches of people and of your own conscience, humbled yourself, and so were freeing yourself from the consequences of sin.
entries.final: — You remembered your sin, bore for it the reproaches of people and of your own conscience, humbled yourself, and so were freeing yourself from the consequences of sin.

entries.russian: — Ты же, — обратился старец к женщине, принесшей назад мелкие камни, — греша мелкими грехами, не помнила их, не каялась в них, привыкла к жизни в грехах и, осуждая грехи других, всё глубже и глубже завязала в своих.
entries.site_before: — But you, — the elder addressed the woman who had brought back the small stones, — by sinning with small sins, did not remember them, did not repent of them, got used to a life in sins, and, condemning the sins of others, became more and more entangled in your own.
entries.repo_before: — But you, — the elder said to the woman who had brought back the small stones, — committing small sins, did not remember them, did not repent of them, grew accustomed to a life in sins and, judging the sins of others, became more and more entangled in your own.
entries.final: — But you, — the elder said to the woman who had brought back the small stones, — committing small sins, did not remember them, did not repent of them, grew accustomed to a life in sins and, judging the sins of others, became more and more entangled in your own.

entries.russian: Все мы грешны, и все мы погибнем, если не будем каяться.
entries.site_before: We are all sinful, and we will all be lost if we do not repent.
entries.repo_before: We are all sinners, and we will all perish if we do not repent.
entries.final: We are all sinners, and we will all perish if we do not repent.

entries.russian: Если есть люди и есть бог, то не может не быть отношения между богом и людьми. И то отношение, которое было в древние времена, не важнее, не обязательнее того, которое есть теперь. Теперешнее отношение понятнее и ближе нам, и потому не теперешнее отношение должно быть проверяемо древним, а наоборот.
entries.site_before: If people exist and God exists, there cannot fail to be a relation between God and people. The relation that existed in ancient times is no more important or binding than the relation that exists now. The present relation is clearer and nearer to us; therefore, the present should not be tested by the ancient, but the ancient by the present.
entries.repo_before: If there are people and there is God, then there cannot fail to be a relation between God and people. And the relation that existed in ancient times is no more important, no more binding than the one that exists now. The present relation is clearer and closer to us, and therefore the present relation should not be tested by the ancient one, but the reverse.
entries.final: If there are people and there is God, then there cannot fail to be a relation between God and people. And the relation that existed in ancient times is no more important, no more binding than the one that exists now. The present relation is clearer and closer to us, and therefore the present relation should not be tested by the ancient one, but the reverse.
entries.reason: P3: а наоборот = "but the reverse" (the site expanded it).

entries.russian: Как удивительно то, что мир терпит и воспринимает из высших откровений истины только самые древние и теперь уже несвоевременные, но всякое прямое откровение, всякую самобытную мысль считает ничтожною и большей частью старательно отвергает.
entries.site_before: How remarkable it is that the world tolerates and accepts from higher revelations of truth only the oldest and now untimely ones, but considers any direct revelation, any original thought, insignificant and mostly diligently rejects it.
entries.repo_before: How remarkable it is that the world tolerates and accepts, of the higher revelations of truth, only the most ancient ones, now already out of date, while it considers every direct revelation, every original thought insignificant and for the most part carefully rejects it.
entries.final: How remarkable it is that the world tolerates and accepts, of the higher revelations of truth, only the most ancient ones, now already out of date, while it considers every direct revelation, every original thought insignificant and for the most part carefully rejects it.

entries.russian: Религиозное сознание человечества не неподвижно, а не переставая изменяется, более и более уясняясь и очищаясь.
entries.site_before: The religious consciousness of humanity is not static, but constantly changes, becoming clearer and purer.
entries.repo_before: The religious consciousness of humanity is not motionless, but changes without ceasing, becoming clearer and purer.
entries.final: The religious consciousness of humanity is not motionless, but changes without ceasing, becoming more and more clear and pure.
entries.reason: T1: более и более = "more and more" (both versions had dropped it).

entries.russian: Одно из самых вредных суеверий есть суеверие о том, что мир сотворен, что он произошел из ничего и что есть бог творящий.
entries.site_before: One of the most harmful superstitions is the superstition that the world was created, that it came from nothing, and that there is a creator God.
entries.repo_before: One of the most harmful superstitions is the superstition that the world was created, that it came from nothing, and that there is a God who creates.
entries.final: One of the most harmful superstitions is the superstition that the world was created, that it came from nothing, and that there is a God who creates.

entries.russian: В сущности мы не имеем никакого основания и никакой нужды предполагать бога-творца (китайцы и индейцы не знают этого понятия), а между тем бог творец и промыслитель несовместим с христианским богом отцом, богом духом, частица которого живет во мне, составляет мою жизнь и проявить и вызвать которую составляет смысл моей жизни, — богом любовью.
entries.site_before: In essence, we have no basis and no need to assume a creator God (the Chinese and Native Americans do not know this concept), and yet the creator and providential God is incompatible with the Christian God the Father, God the Spirit, a particle of whom lives in me, makes up my life, and manifesting and bringing forth which constitutes the meaning of my life — God of love.
entries.repo_before: In essence we have no basis and no need to suppose a creator God (the Chinese and Indians do not know this concept), and yet God the creator and providential ruler is incompatible with the Christian God the Father, God the Spirit, a particle of whom lives in me, constitutes my life, and to manifest and call forth which constitutes the meaning of my life—with God as love.
entries.final: In essence we have no basis and no need to suppose a creator God (the Chinese and the American Indians do not know this concept), and yet God the creator and providential ruler is incompatible with the Christian God the Father, God the Spirit, a particle of whom lives in me, constitutes my life, and to manifest and call forth which constitutes the meaning of my life—with God who is love.
entries.reason: Repo wording; индейцы = "American Indians" (not India); богом любовью = "God who is love".

entries.russian: Бог творец равнодушен и допускает страдание и зло. Бог дух избавляет от страдания и зла и есть всегда совершенное благо.
entries.site_before: The creator God is indifferent and permits suffering and evil. God the Spirit frees from suffering and evil and is always perfect good.
entries.repo_before: God the creator is indifferent and permits suffering and evil. God the Spirit delivers from suffering and evil and is always perfect good.
entries.final: God the creator is indifferent and permits suffering and evil. God the Spirit delivers from suffering and evil and is always perfect good.

entries.russian: Есть я, познающий мир данными мне орудиями чувств и знающий внутренно своего отца бога, но бога творца я не знаю и не могу знать.
entries.site_before: There is I, who perceives the world with the instruments of sense given to me and knows inwardly my Father God, but I do not know the creator God and cannot know Him.
entries.repo_before: I exist, knowing the world through the instruments of the senses given to me and inwardly knowing my Father God, but God the creator I do not know and cannot know.
entries.final: I exist, knowing the world through the instruments of the senses given to me and inwardly knowing my Father God, but God the creator I do not know and cannot know.

entries.russian: Есть много хорошего и в Коране, и в буддийских, и в конфуцианских книгах, и в писаниях стоиков, и в Библии, и в Упанишадах, и в Евангелии, но больше всего нужного и понятного в ближайших нам религиозных мыслителях.
entries.site_before: There is much good in the Quran, and in Buddhist and Confucian books, and in the writings of the Stoics, and in the Bible, and in the Upanishads, and in the Gospel, but the most necessary and understandable is found in the religious thinkers closest to us.
entries.repo_before: There is much that is good in the Koran, in Buddhist and Confucian books, in the writings of the Stoics, in the Bible, in the Upanishads, and in the Gospel, but most of what is necessary and understandable is in the religious thinkers nearest to us.
entries.final: There is much that is good in the Quran, and in Buddhist and Confucian books, and in the writings of the Stoics, and in the Bible, and in the Upanishads, and in the Gospel, but most of what is necessary and understandable is in the religious thinkers nearest to us.
entries.reason: Repo wording; T3 keeps the repeated и в ("and in"); Quran per the book's modern name forms.

entries.russian: Когда кто-либо привязывается к одной какой-нибудь, хотя бы и верной, идее, то он в сущности попадает в то же положение, в каком находился бы человек, привязавший себя к столбу, для того, чтобы не заблудиться. То, что может быть желанной истиной на известной ступени духовного роста, может быть помехой к этому росту и заблуждением на другой, более высокой ступени.
entries.site_before: When someone becomes attached to any one idea, even a correct one, they essentially end up in the same position as a person who tied themselves to a post in order not to get lost. What may be a desired truth at a certain stage of spiritual growth may become an obstacle to this growth and a delusion at another, higher stage.
entries.repo_before: When someone attaches himself to any one idea, even a true one, he essentially puts himself in the same position as a person who tied himself to a post so as not to lose his way. What may be a desirable truth at a certain stage of spiritual growth may become an obstacle to that growth and an error at another, higher stage.
entries.final: When someone attaches himself to any one idea, even a true one, he essentially puts himself in the same position as a person who tied himself to a post so as not to lose his way. What may be a desirable truth at a certain stage of spiritual growth may become an obstacle to that growth and an error at another, higher stage.
